August 25, 2026

Supreme Court lifts injunction on Trump's election executive order

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

The Supreme Court, in a 6-3 decision, stayed an injunction that had blocked large parts of President Trump's election-related executive order, allowing provisions such as the creation of a citizenship database to take effect while litigation continues. The order does not touch a separate injunction covering whether the U.S. Postal Service may send mail-in ballots to states. Justice Jackson warned in dissent that the ruling would foment chaos and confusion ahead of November's elections. It is unclear whether the Court will rule on the merits before the vote.

State Department prepares revocation of up to 200,000 visas

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Associated Press has confirmed that the State Department, working with the Department of Homeland Security, plans to revoke as many as 200,000 B1 and B2 business and tourism visas at once. The visas were granted between 2016 and 2026 to people who have sought or are currently seeking asylum in the United States. It would be the largest mass revocation of visas in American history, and is expected to face court challenges.

Judge finds ICE agents violated order barring enforcement in places of worship

tags: immigration, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

A federal judge in Minneapolis ruled that ICE agents violated his order prohibiting immigration enforcement inside places of worship. As part of an operation called Operation Puppet Master, agents went undercover inside the University Baptist gymnasium on at least one occasion, ran license plates of churchgoers, and waited outside to observe people entering and leaving. The Department of Homeland Security may face contempt proceedings over the violations.

Iranian state media places $10 million bounty on Barron Trump

tags: politics, war
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Iranian state media has announced a $10 million bounty on the life of Barron Trump, the president's son. The move is being characterized as a significant escalation by Iran amid ongoing hostilities with the United States.

Iran seen holding escalation options well beyond the Strait of Hormuz

tags: war, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

Iran retains several avenues to escalate should U.S. economic pressure intensify, ranging from disruption at the Strait of Hormuz to cyberattacks. Oil exports and Gulf shipping are among the pressure points identified. The assessment indicates the consequences of any Iranian response would extend far beyond the strait itself.

Air Force major charged under rare military statute after impeachment call

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Major Jason Watson, described as the first active-duty U.S. service member to publicly call for President Trump's impeachment and removal, has been charged with multiple criminal offenses, including counts under Article 88 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice. Only two other prosecutions under that article have been brought since 1951. Watson, who also called for the vice president's impeachment over the war in Iran, is being held in solitary-confinement conditions according to his attorney and faces the possibility of years in prison.

Judge denies Ghislaine Maxwell's habeas petition

tags: legal, epstein
sources: @aaronparnas

Judge Engelmayer of the Southern District of New York rejected Ghislaine Maxwell's habeas corpus petition, her final legal avenue for early release. She has roughly 13 to 15 years remaining on her sentence. With no legal options left, a presidential pardon would be the only remaining route out of prison, and there are currently no indications one will be granted.

Canada readies dollar-for-dollar tariffs as Trump floats renaming Lake Ontario

tags: markets, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Canada is preparing to announce dollar-for-dollar retaliatory tariffs against the United States as the trade dispute between the two countries escalates. President Trump said he is giving serious consideration to renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America, saying the U.S. "won't be doing much business with Ontario anymore." The remarks followed Ontario Premier Doug Ford telling Trump he could "kiss his ass."

Senators demand answers over extended Iran deployments

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Lawmakers are pressing the Pentagon for explanations about extended deployments tied to operations involving Iran. The extensions are affecting troops across the force. Members of the Senate have demanded answers on the scope and duration of the deployments.

Russia warns Britain over new missile support for Ukraine

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Russia issued a warning to Britain over new missile support being provided to Ukraine. Moscow said London is "adding fuel to the fire" with the additional military assistance.

US military aircraft tracked landing in Russia amid reports CIA director aboard

tags: politics, war
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A U.S. Air Force C-17 Globemaster was tracked flying over Moscow and landing in Russia. It is alleged that CIA Director John Ratcliffe was aboard the aircraft. Neither the Kremlin nor Washington has issued an official statement about the flight, though the flight track is publicly viewable.

Reporting ties Andy Biggs to killing bill targeting FLDS enforcement arm

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

New reporting concerning Arizona Republican gubernatorial candidate and congressman Andy Biggs says he killed a bipartisan bill in 2013 that would have shut down a marshal's office acting as the enforcement arm of the FLDS in Colorado City, Arizona. Newly unearthed footage shows Biggs saying he was not concerned that his decision allowed abuse there to continue. A mini documentary released detailing the episode could affect the state's governor's race.

Secret Service ordered live stream cameras off Trump at Washington IndyCar race

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas

During a live stream of the IndyCar Grand Prix in Washington, D.C., the White House and Secret Service instructed a camera operator to stop filming President Trump, with an audible instruction that the cameras be taken off the president. The operator complied and moved the cameras away. The president was filmed at other points during the event, and the White House has not explained the instruction.

White House Instagram account posts 'Magic Deportation Bus' meme

tags: politics, immigration, media
sources: @aaronparnas

The official White House Instagram account published a meme parodying The Magic School Bus, titled the "Magic Deportation Bus," depicting detained migrants in chains. The image appears on a government-run account used by members of the public, including children, to find information about the federal government.

Air Force awards Boeing F-15 contract with $131 billion ceiling

tags: defence, markets
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Air Force has awarded Boeing a new F-15 contract carrying a ceiling of more than $131 billion. The award covers continued production and support of the aircraft.

Navy unveils long-range 'Malice' air-to-air missile

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Navy revealed a new air-to-air missile designated "Malice." The weapon weighs roughly 1,500 pounds and has a stated range beyond 250 nautical miles.

Nearly 1,300 Navy family members barred from returning to Bahrain

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

About 1,300 family members of Navy personnel have been told they cannot return to Bahrain for the foreseeable future. The restriction leaves families separated from service members stationed in the region indefinitely.

Gaza parents urged to keep children from flying kites after Israeli threat

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Parents in Gaza have been urged to stop their children from flying kites after Israel threatened a forceful response to the activity. The warning was relayed to families in the territory.

Air Guard and Reserve face August 31 deadline under new fitness standards

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

New Air Force fitness standards will make waist-to-height ratio count for 20 percent of a member's fitness score. Air National Guard and Reserve personnel face an August 31 deadline under the revised measurement requirements.

Navy families at Norfolk report power outages lasting up to 15 hours

tags: defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

Families living in Navy housing at Norfolk say repeated power outages have lasted as long as 15 hours. Residents report being left without air conditioning and losing food to spoilage.

Analyst says Treasury debt buybacks signal move toward yield curve control

tags: markets, economy
sources: @ericmoutsos

A monetary analyst argued that the U.S. Treasury issuing new debt to purchase existing debt is an early sign of yield curve control, a policy last used domestically during World War II when spending surged and buyers of debt were scarce. The claim is that officials and media will characterize the operation as distinct from quantitative easing and non-inflationary, but that the historical precedent was followed by inflation reaching 18 percent. Because the debt today is roughly ten times its World War II level in inflation-adjusted terms, the argument holds that any resulting inflation would be substantially worse.

Claim links data center buildout to automated controls on digital transactions

tags: surveillance, tech
sources: @ericmoutsos

An argument circulating holds that the purpose of large-scale data centers and AI infrastructure in North America is to enable an "automatic third lock" on currency, bank deposits, and securities — a system that would let authorities block or condition transactions without a bank intermediary. The comparison drawn is to Canadian banks freezing trucker convoy accounts under government direction, described as a manual version of the same mechanism. The claim is that an automated version could implement a social credit system with individualized rules, negative interest rates, or tax changes, and that surveillance video and financial transaction data together require the computing capacity being built.
